:::{#thm-loglik-iid}

#### Log-likelihood of an independent sample

For mutually independent data $X_1, \ldots, X_n$:

$$\ell(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n \log{\p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta)}$$ {#eq-loglik-ind}

If the $X_i$ also share a common distribution $\p(X = x \mid \theta)$,
each term is $\log{\p(X = x_i \mid \theta)}$.
:::

:::{.proof}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell(\theta)
&\eqdef \log{\Lik(\theta)}
&& \text{(definition of log-likelihood)}\\
&= \log{\prod_{i=1}^n \p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta)}
&& \text{(likelihood of an independent sample)}\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \log{\p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta)}
&& \text{(log of a product is a sum of logs)}
\end{aligned}
$$

With a common distribution, $\p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta) = \p(X = x_i \mid \theta)$.
:::
